title: Nanoburst falloff — scratchpad and run log
content:
Context / motivation:
- Observed intermittent p99 spikes in prod when very short, high-intensity ingress waves hit an otherwise idle pod pool. Pattern looks like a sharp throughput spike followed by exponential-like decay ('falloff') back to baseline even when load continues at lower QPS.
- Hypothesis: a combination of KV-cache cold misses + scheduler preemption + one-shot kernel warm paths causes a transient window of reduced per-token throughput and inflated latency tail.

Objective:
- Characterize the "falloff" half-life (time until throughput drops by 50% from peak) for different burst shapes and backend states.
- Test mitigation vectors: aggressive cache prefill, ramped ingress shaping, pro-active warm mini-batches.

Test harness and commands:
- Load generator: local redwood-loadgen v0.19 (custom) with modes: step, sawtooth, nanoburst.
- Invocations used (example):
  redwood-loadgen --mode nanoburst --qps-peak 1800 --peak-duration 3s --sustain-qps 200 --sustain-duration 120s --seq-len 128 --model rwd-open-3b-q4_0 --concurrency 256 --target-endpoint https://hosted.redwood/api/v1/generate | tee run-nb-20250115.log
- Also used wrk-style generator for comparison:
  wrk -t8 -c400 -d180s --script=nanoburst.lua http://local-proxy:8080

Environment and baseline:
- Dedicated m G4dn-like nodes (8x A100 style simulated), single model shard, quantized (q4_0).
- Backend runtime: serving-runtime v2.3.0-rc (kernel preemption branch toggled on for some runs).
- Baseline: warm cache, steady 200 qps -> stable p50 12ms, p95 45ms, p99 110ms.

Key runs (selection):
- Run A (cold-ish start, no prefill): peak 1800 qps for 3s -> sustain 200qps for 120s.
  Observed: immediate p99 spike to 2200ms at t=0.8s, throughput peaked ~1.5s then decayed with half-life ~9s, reached steady-state throughput ~210 qps at t~28s.

- Run B (prefill KV cache 30s @ 400 qps before nanoburst):
  Observed: peak p99 reduced to 450ms, half-life ~4s, throughput recovered to steady 200 qps by ~11s.

- Run C (ramped ingress: ramp to 600 qps over 1s then step to 1800 qps):
  Observed: somewhat less severe p99 peaks (max ~980ms), half-life ~6s.

- Run D (enable proactive warm mini-batch = 8 micro-batches during peak):
  Observed: p99 ~520ms, half-life ~3s, but throughput during peak was slightly lower (~1650 qps) due to warm batch injection overhead.

Representative numbers (rough):
- Metric table (avg across 3 repeats):
  Mode      | peak-p99 (ms) | half-life (s) | steady-throughput (qps) | notes
  --------------------------------------------------------------
  cold      | 2200          | 9.1           | 210                     | no prefill
  prefill   | 450           | 3.9           | 205                     | KV primed
  ramped    | 980           | 6.2           | 198                     | gentler slope
  warm-mini | 520           | 3.2           | 165                     | overhead tradeoff

Diagnosis notes / signals observed:
- KV cache miss rate correlates tightly with peak p99 and with observed half-life. Misses cluster in the first 1–5s after burst.
- GPU kernel churn: we saw a higher rate of schedule preemptions logged by runtime at t=0..2s in cold runs. Corresponds to large absolute latency moments.
- Tokenization + CPU parse spikes also present for very short bursts (single-request fanout causes small bursts of CPU pressure).
- Queueing distribution: during decay window there is a persistent small queue (~20–40 requests) being serviced with longer service times; suggests degraded per-token throughput rather than simple queuing backlog.

Quick conclusions so far:
1) The falloff behavior appears multi-factor: KV-cache cold misses are major contributor; kernel warmup/path selection and brief scheduler preemption amplify it.
2) Simple prefill reduces both peak and falloff half-life the most, with minimal steady-state cost.
3) Ramping ingress is effective but not always feasible for real traffic.
4) Proactive warm-mini-batch works but trades peak throughput for lower tail — might be acceptable for SLO vs QPS tradeoffs.

Micro-actions / next experiments:
- Run an FFT on p99 time-series across runs to identify dominant frequencies from microbursts (useful for shaping/TTL decisions). (Command: python analysis/fft_p99.py run-nb-20250115.log)
- Test targeted KV prefill: prime only top-k prefixes observed in production burst logs to see if smaller priming budget gives most benefit.
- Try alternate scheduling policy on runtime (favor long-lived kernels during bursts) — ephemeral branch available in infra.
- Cost analysis: quantify token-cost increase for warm-mini-batch vs saved error budget from reduced p99.
- Instrument the client/proxy to add a short-lived 50–100ms ramp when it detects burst signature.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is there an interaction with autoscaler delay? if pods scale down aggressively then we get more cold state. Need to reproduce with pod churn.
- Confirm whether quantization variant (q4_0 vs q4_1) materially changes kernel warmup penalty.
- Check effect of concurrency limit per-pod: in some runs lowering concurrency reduced tail (less contention), in others it just lowered throughput uniformly.

Raw snippets from logs (trimmed):
[2025-01-15 14:03:12] peak qps ~1789, p99 2187ms, kv_miss_rate 0.87
[2025-01-15 14:03:21] p99 1360ms, kv_miss_rate 0.52
[2025-01-15 14:03:30] p99 410ms, kv_miss_rate 0.12

Notes on reproducibility:
- Seeds: loadgen has nondet scheduling; repeat each config 3x and capture full telemetry.
- Save runtime metrics (kernel switches, preempt counts) with sampling at 100ms resolution.
- Annotate runs with git commit id and feature flags (we did this in linked_artifacts PR#214).

Immediate recommendation (for product):
- Ship a lightweight prefill strategy to Dedicated customers behind a toggle: when a route sees a new cold window (idle > Xs) automatically run a small priming at low QPS to reduce next-burst tail.

Next steps (who):
- (Cassidy) implement targeted prefill runner + automation on load-detection hook (2 days prototype).
- (Arjun) surface kernel preemption metrics in console dashboard per-route (1 week).
- (Lena) run cost/benefit analysis for warm-mini-batch vs prefill (2 days).

Scratchpad end.
